Answer: D
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 2) demonstrates an ill-defined, patchy parenchymal consolidation in the left lower lobe with visible air bronchograms and a subpleural/peribronchial distribution. This radiographic pattern, combined with the clinical history of persistent infiltrates unresponsive to antibiotics, is classic for Bronchiolitis Obliterans Organizing Pneumonia (BOOP), also known as Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP).
